title: Headless signing pre-launch probe false-passes via launcher ssh-agent; sandboxed worker then cannot sign
body:
## What happened

A headless worker (v3.37.30) was launched, finished its implementation, then failed at `git commit` with `Load key ...: incorrect passphrase supplied to decrypt private key` and exited `BLOCKED ... TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=permission_required`. The pre-launch signing check had passed, so the worker was allowed to start even though it could never sign.

## Root cause (verified)

1. `headless-runtime-helper.sh:38-43` sources `~/.ssh/agent.env`, so the **launcher** has `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` pointing at an agent holding the user's passphrase-protected interactive key.
2. `headless-runtime-attempt.sh:79-84` (`_configure_headless_worker_signing_env`): when the dedicated key `~/.ssh/id_ed25519_signing.pub` is absent, it runs `_headless_worker_signing_commit_probe` (lines 44-55) **in the launcher environment**. The probe succeeds through the launcher's agent socket, and the function marks signing configured without adding process-scoped config (the GH#29902 "proven pre-existing setup" path).
3. The worker then runs inside the clean sandbox. `_headless_sandbox_passthrough_names` in `headless-runtime-lib.sh:889-916` ends with `*) continue`, and `sandbox-exec-helper.sh:54` `DEFAULT_PASSTHROUGH="PATH HOME USER LANG TERM SHELL"`. Neither passes `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`. Inside the sandbox, `ssh-keygen -Y sign` falls back to the encrypted private key file and fails.

So the probe checks a different environment from the one the worker commits in. It gives a false pass exactly when no dedicated headless key exists.

## Expected

Either (a) the probe runs with the same environment the sandboxed worker gets (the sandbox env set, no `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`), so a missing dedicated key fails pre-launch with the existing message "run 'aidevops signing headless-setup'"; or (b) `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` is deliberately passed through when the proven setup relies on an agent. Option (a) matches the fail-closed design already in `_prepare_headless_worker_signing` (headless-runtime-attempt.sh:96-122).

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-attempt.sh:44-91` — probe and configure path
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh:889-916` — sandbox passthrough allowlist
- `.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh:54` — default passthrough

## Verification

- Reproduce: global `commit.gpgsign=true`, `gpg.format=ssh`, `user.signingkey=<passphrase-protected key>.pub`, key loaded in the agent referenced by `~/.ssh/agent.env`, and no `~/.ssh/id_ed25519_signing`. Dispatch a worker. Today it launches and fails at commit; after the fix it must fail pre-launch with `worker_signing_unavailable`.
- With a dedicated key from `aidevops signing headless-setup`, the worker must still sign successfully.
- Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-contract-tests.sh` for the absent-key and agent-only case.

## What happened

On a system where headless workers could not sign (see the companion issue about the signing pre-launch false pass), earlier workers "succeeded" by disabling signing per command. `quality-hooks.log` records worker Git operations such as:

- In a headless worker with signing required, `git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit ...` and `git commit --no-gpg-sign ...` are rejected with an actionable message naming `aidevops signing headless-setup`.

title: Canonical Git guard blocks git config --global key reads; signing-setup.sh check falsely reports signing not set
body:
## What happened

Inside an agent session whose cwd is a canonical repository checkout, `signing-setup.sh check` reports:

```
gpg.format:      not set
user.signingkey: not set
commit.gpgsign:  not set
[WARN] SSH commit signing is not fully configured
Run: aidevops signing setup
```

However, global signing **is** configured, and commits sign correctly.

## Root cause (verified with `bash -x`)

`signing-setup.sh:72-75` reads values with `git config --global <key> 2>/dev/null || echo "not set"`. In agent sessions, `git` resolves to the aidevops Git shim (`agents/scripts/git`). The canonical Git guard treats a single-key read, `git config --global gpg.format`, as a mutation and exits 42:

```
BLOCKED by canonical Git guard: canonical worktree mutation via 'git config'. ...
exit=42
```

`2>/dev/null` hides that, and the fallback prints "not set". By contrast, `git config --global --list` and `git config --global --show-origin gpg.format` are allowed and return the real values. This sends users and agents after a nonexistent configuration problem, and it prompts `aidevops signing setup`, which rewrites global config.

## Expected

1. The canonical Git guard should classify `git config [--global|--system|--file X] [--get|--get-all|--get-regexp|--list|--show-origin|<key>]` (no value argument, no `--unset`, `--add`, `--replace-all`, `--edit` or `--rename-section`) as a read. `--global` and `--system` reads never mutate the worktree.
2. `signing-setup.sh` should use `--get` explicitly and distinguish exit 1 (key unset) from other failures, reporting "unable to read git config (exit N)" instead of "not set".

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/git` shim / canonical guard classification of `git config`
- `.agents/scripts/signing-setup.sh:72-75` and the same pattern at lines 138, 199, 218 and 387

## Verification

- From a canonical checkout inside an agent session: `git config --global gpg.format` prints the value and exits 0. `git config --global gpg.format ssh` is still blocked.
- `signing-setup.sh check` reports the real configured values.
- Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-signing-setup.sh` and the shim's guard tests.

body:
## What

Attribute the ~48% of REST-core HTTP attempts that `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log` records under the generic caller `gh_api_rest`, so REST volume can be reduced where it originates.

## Why

On a maintainer runner that uses one PAT, REST-core demand is the binding API constraint. `gh_transport_capacity.py:54-69` paces only when observed demand would exhaust the remaining quota before reset. The draft PR for #33062 (#33063) measured deliberate pacing of 0.4–5.9 s per call under 6-way concurrency, which dwarfs mechanical shim overhead. Cutting request **volume** is therefore the main lever. It needs attribution first.

Evidence from the last 12 h (2026-09-29 06:50Z → 18:50Z), REST-core `attempt` rows:

- 44,085 attempts, about 3,700–4,150 per full hour against the 5,000/h limit (a steady 75–83%).
- By caller: `gh_api_rest` 21,111 (47.9%), `pulse-wrapper.sh` 9,092 (20.6%), `pulse-merge-routine.sh` 2,871 (6.5%), `review-bot-gate-helper.sh` 2,152 (4.9%), `post-merge-review-scanner.sh` 1,500 (3.4%), and others below 3% each.
- `gh_api_rest` by site tag: `rest-core-gh-pat` 12,247, `rest-response-owned` 2,741, `pulse-review-explicit-page` 2,562, `explicit-rest-pagination` 1,640, `rest-core-selected` 1,110.

Cause: `_shim_transport_caller_label` (`.agents/scripts/gh-native-transport-lib.sh:173-185`) uses `AIDEVOPS_GH_CALLER`, but only when it names a framework script file (`_shim_framework_caller_label`, lines 129-137). Otherwise it uses the parent process command (`_shim_parent_framework_caller`, lines 139-171), and finally falls back to the subcommand label `gh_api_rest` (line 120). Model-driven calls from headless workers, the pulse LLM phase and interactive sessions run under runtime shells whose parent command is not a framework script. They therefore can't be distinguished from each other or from framework subshells that lose the caller. The `pulse-review-explicit-page` tag under `gh_api_rest` suggests at least one framework path also loses its caller.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
awk -F'\t' -v c="$(( $(date +%s) - 43200 ))" '$1>=c && $5=="rest-core" && $9=="attempt" {n++; if ($2=="gh_api_rest") g++} END {printf "rest-core=%d gh_api_rest=%d (%.1f%%)\n", n, g, 100*g/n}' ~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log
```

**Actual output**: `rest-core=44085 gh_api_rest=21111 (47.9%)`

**Blocked command**: `gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/1 --jq .number` through the shim, 6 concurrent reads (#33063 measurements): wall 1,465–7,001 ms, of which deliberate primary pacing was 396–5,921 ms; native child `gh` 377–555 ms.

**Backend state**: single `gh-pat` identity; REST-core attempts of 3,674/h on average and 3,564–4,151 per full hour over the last 12 h (limit 5,000/h). Hourly minimum observed `x-ratelimit-remaining` was as low as 560 in a 26 h window on 2026-09-28/29. Pacing reason `local primary pacing from observed demand and reset` (`gh_transport_capacity.py:11`).

**Expected**: at most 10% of REST-core attempts carry a generic subcommand label. The rest name a framework script or a bounded session role.

## How

1. Add a small allowlist of session-role caller labels accepted from `AIDEVOPS_GH_CALLER` in addition to framework script basenames, for example `worker`, `pulse-llm`, `interactive`, `routine`. Values must be validated against the allowlist and never taken verbatim from untrusted input, to prevent log injection.
2. Export the role where sessions start: headless worker and pulse launches (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` and its worker preparation path) and interactive runtime session setup. Where a worker's issue is known, record the role only; issue numbers belong in existing worker telemetry, not the caller field.
3. Find the framework path behind `pulse-review-explicit-page` rows labelled `gh_api_rest` (`rg -n "pulse-review-explicit-page" .agents/scripts`) and propagate `AIDEVOPS_GH_CALLER` there.
4. Consider caching the parent-caller lookup per process. `_shim_parent_framework_caller` currently spawns `ps` on every call, which also adds to #33062's mechanical overhead.
5. Do not change quota admission, pacing or trust behaviour.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-prepare.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/gh-api-instrument.sh`
- Unknown until step 3: the framework script emitting `pulse-review-explicit-page` REST calls.

## Acceptance

title: t18554: fix(release): unshallow the release control worktree before lane reservation so a shallow store cannot strand the release lane
body:
## What

Make `aidevops release` handle a shallow shared object store before it reserves the release lane. It should self-heal through a bounded `git fetch --unshallow --tags origin` in its own control linked worktree, the same way `full-loop-helper-commit.sh` does. If healing is disabled or fails, it should stop with an actionable `RELEASE_SHALLOW_STORE` error before any lane write. Today the helper dies on a raw `git describe` error after reserving the lane, and that strands the lane for five minutes.

## Why

- **Observed 2026-09-29.** `aidevops release patch 33042 incremental` exited 1 after 25s:
  - it failed at phase `release-run-new` with `fatal: No tags can describe '2523f44c…'`;
  - the failing call is `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh:346` (`git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --abbrev=0 "$snapshot"`);
  - the canonical aidevops store was shallow, with 19 reachable commits, after the claim-path depth fetches fixed by GH#33033.
- **The failure stranded the lane.**
  - `release_lane_acquire` (L667) had already reserved the lane, so `aidevops release status` showed `phase:"reserved"` and `RELEASE_EXECUTOR={"state":"dead"}`.
  - The rerun exited 8, and `recover-reservation` refused until the five-minute window passed.
  - One manual `git fetch --unshallow --tags origin` from a linked worktree (18s) healed the store, and v3.37.31 was then tagged normally.
- **The fix is cheap and has precedent.**
  - The helper already runs git in a disposable control linked worktree (`REPO_ROOT`, set by `_full_loop_release_prepare_control_worktree`, L88-111), so an unshallow there uses the documented linked-worktree route in `.agents/reference/git-hygiene.md`.
  - `_check_and_handle_shallow_clone` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh:1263-1302` is the reference pattern, including the `AIDEVOPS_SHALLOW_UNSHALLOW=0` opt-out.
- **Shallow stores can still happen.** GH#33033 removes one cause, but older deployed copies, `--depth` clones and other tools can still produce them. The release path should not depend on every other writer behaving.

1. In `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh`, add `_full_loop_release_ensure_full_history` next to `_full_loop_release_prepare_new` (L325). Model it on `_check_and_handle_shallow_clone`:
   - it returns 0 unless `git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` prints exactly `true`;
   - when `AIDEVOPS_SHALLOW_UNSHALLOW=0`, it prints `RELEASE_SHALLOW_STORE action=disabled` plus the manual command, and returns 1;
   - otherwise it runs `timeout_sec "${AIDEVOPS_RELEASE_UNSHALLOW_TIMEOUT_S:-600}" git -C "$REPO_ROOT" fetch --unshallow --tags origin` (`timeout_sec` is from the already-sourced `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh:708`), then re-checks and prints `RELEASE_SHALLOW_STORE action=healed` or `action=failed`.
2. Call it at the top of `_full_loop_release_start_new` (L623-634), before `_full_loop_release_guard_competing_lane`, so a failure never reserves, recovers or writes the lane.
3. As defence in depth at L346, when `git describe` fails, print `RELEASE_BASE_TAG_UNRESOLVED snapshot=<sha> shallow=<true|false>` and a pointer to `git fetch --unshallow --tags origin` before `return 1`.
4. Add a Troubleshooting row to `.agents/workflows/release.md:321-330` (`fatal: No tags can describe` / `RELEASE_SHALLOW_STORE`) and one sentence to `.agents/reference/git-hygiene.md` saying the release helper self-heals too.
5. Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-helper.sh`:
   - add stub cases to its `git` stub (L18-47): `*--is-shallow-repository*` prints `${FAKE_SHALLOW:-false}`, and `*fetch\ --unshallow*` logs the call and exits `${FAKE_UNSHALLOW_EXIT:-0}`;
   - add three scenarios:

     - shallow with `AIDEVOPS_SHALLOW_UNSHALLOW=0`: non-zero exit, `RELEASE_SHALLOW_STORE action=disabled`, and no `LANE_STATE_FILE` written;

title: t18555: fix(dispatch-dedup): merged-PR keyword check ignores issue reopen, permanently blocking reopened issues
body:
## What

`has_open_pr` Check 2 (`_has_open_pr_check_merged_keywords`, `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh:640-673`) treats any merged PR whose body has a closing keyword for issue #N as permanent "already solved" evidence. It does not consider that the issue was **reopened after** that PR merged. As a result, every legitimately reopened issue is dedup-blocked forever.

## Why (evidence)

Canonical file-size-debt issue #28839 was solved by PR #28845 (merged 2026-07-29). The file then grew back to 2,034 lines, and `_large_file_gate_reopen_debt_issue` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh:621-637`) reopened #28839 by design ("Reusing the durable issue identity prevents close/create/auto-dispatch loops"). From then on, every pulse cycle logged:

```
[pulse-wrapper] Dedup: merged PR #28845 references issue #28839 via keyword issue=#28839 repo=marcusquinn/aidevops
[dispatch_with_dedup] DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=dedup_active_claim signal=dedup_guard_blocked issue=#28839

```

`pulse-diagnose-helper.sh issue 28839` counted **386** dedup blocks, each taking ~27 s of dispatch time (`elapsed_ms=26843`). The reopened debt issue also held #32638 (dispatch-ceremony performance) behind `needs-simplification` indefinitely. The same pattern affects any reopened issue that has an earlier merged `Resolves #N` PR, not just file-size debt.

A secondary, cosmetic symptom: `_large_file_gate_normalize_debt_issue` (`pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh:564-586`) does not remove the stale `solved:worker` label on reopen.

## How

1. In `_has_open_pr_check_merged_keywords`, request `mergedAt` alongside `number,body`. If a closing-keyword match exists, fetch the issue's latest `reopened` event time with one bounded REST call, **only on this matched path**: `gh api "repos/${repo_slug}/issues/${issue_number}/events?per_page=100"`, then select `event=="reopened"` and take the max `created_at`. Ignore matches whose `mergedAt` is earlier than that time. Return evidence only for merged PRs at or after the last reopen.
2. If the events lookup fails, emit `_ddpr_emit_lookup_uncertain` as the other checks do (fail closed, no dispatch).
3. In `_large_file_gate_normalize_debt_issue`, add `--remove-label "solved:worker"`, and any other `solved:*` label that exists in that helper's taxonomy (check `rg -n "solved:" .agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh .agents/scripts/*label*`).
4. Keep every other dedup check unchanged.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-helper-has-open-pr.sh

## Reference pattern

Model the uncertain-lookup handling on `_has_open_pr_check_open_body_keyword` (`dispatch-dedup-pr.sh:591-624`, `_ddpr_emit_lookup_uncertain`). Extend the existing merged-keyword fixture in `test-dispatch-dedup-helper-has-open-pr.sh` (around line 312) with a reopened-after-merge case.

## Acceptance

- A merged `Resolves #N` PR merged **before** the issue's latest reopen no longer blocks dispatch. One merged **after** the latest reopen still blocks.
- An events lookup failure yields `PR_LOOKUP_RESULT=uncertain` (no dispatch).
- The existing tests `test-dispatch-dedup-helper-has-open-pr.sh`, `test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection.sh`, and `test-large-file-gate-continuation-verify.sh` pass.

## Verification

title: t18556: fix(release): look up the tag-push publish run by exact head_sha and skip recovery dispatch when channels are already published
body:
## What

Stop `aidevops release reconcile` from dispatching a redundant recovery publish when GitHub's workflow-run list returns a stale or partial page:

- Look up the tag-push publish run by exact `head_sha`, not by scanning the whole `event=push` history.
- Treat "no run found" as a reason to dispatch only when the release channels are not already published for that tag.

## Why

- **Observed 2026-09-29 (v3.37.31).**
  - Push run `36617731862` (`event=push`, `head_branch=v3.37.31`, `head_sha=8fe6334e…`, `success`) was created at 19:13:43Z.
  - About ten minutes later, `aidevops release reconcile 33042` classified the workflow as `absent` (rc 3) and dispatched recovery run `36618899675` at 19:23:29Z.
  - The GitHub release, npm `3.37.31` and Homebrew `3.37.31` were already published, so the recovery publish was redundant. It succeeded idempotently, but cost a full publish run and a second reconcile cycle.
- **Root cause: the list endpoint is not a reliable absence signal.**
  - `_full_loop_release_find_workflow_run` (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh:599-646`) fetches `actions/workflows/publish-packages.yml/runs` with `-f event=push -F per_page=100 --paginate` (L616-617), then selects `head_branch == tag and head_sha == tag_commit` in jq (L633).
  - A read-only replay of that exact query returned one page of only 22 push runs, none of them for `v3.37.31`.
  - One repeat through native `gh` 2.101.0 returned `total_count:140`, with the newest run from 2026-09-16. The same filter in URL form returned `total_count:249` with `v3.37.31` first, and later repeats of both forms returned 249.
  - So the event-filtered list intermittently serves stale snapshots. `_full_loop_release_inspect_remote` (L950-965) turns that into rc 3, and L1577-1580 then dispatches recovery.
- **An exact lookup exists.** `gh api --method GET repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/workflows/publish-packages.yml/runs -f event=push -f head_sha=<tag_commit>` returned exactly `total_count:1`, run `36617731862`. `.agents/scripts/postflight-check.sh:144-145` already uses a `head_sha` run query.

## How

1. In `_full_loop_release_find_workflow_run` (L616-617), add `-f head_sha="$tag_commit"` to the push-event query. Keep `--paginate`, `-F per_page=100` and the jq selection unchanged, so the tag-ref binding at L633 still applies.
   - Do not add `head_sha` to the `workflow_dispatch` query (L618-619). Recovery runs execute on a `main` commit, not the tag commit, and are correlated by display title at L634-638.
2. In `_full_loop_release_inspect_remote` (L960-964), when `find_rc` is 3:
   - first call `_full_loop_release_verify_channels "$repo" "$tag_name"`. It reads the release, npm and Homebrew state and does not use `_FULL_LOOP_RELEASE_RUN_JSON`;
   - if channels verify, print `RELEASE_TAG=…`, `WORKFLOW_STATUS=absent` and `WORKFLOW_LOOKUP=uncorroborated`, then return 8 (pending, no dispatch). The next reconcile finds the run through the exact lookup;
   - if channels do not verify, keep today's output and return 3, so a genuinely missing publication still dispatches recovery.
3. Tests:
   - `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile-channels.sh`: make the `gh` stub's push branch (L49-53) return run `10` only when `$args` contains ` -f head_sha=3333333333333333333333333333333333333333 `, and an empty `workflow_runs` array otherwise. The existing PASS lines then prove that the exact filter is sent. Keep the `oversized` mode (L28-43) working; it only checks for `--paginate`, `-F per_page=100` and ` -f event=push `.
   - `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile.sh` inline boundary block (L26-65): add two scenarios in which `_full_loop_release_find_workflow_run` returns 3.
     - When `_full_loop_release_verify_channels` returns 0, inspect returns 8, prints `WORKFLOW_LOOKUP=uncorroborated`, and `grace-dispatch.log` gains no line.
     - When it returns 1, inspect returns 3.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile-channels.sh
- TODO.md

## Acceptance

- The push-run lookup sends `-f head_sha=<tag_commit>` and still requires `head_branch == <tag>`.
- If no run is found but channels already verify for the tag, reconcile returns 8 with `WORKFLOW_LOOKUP=uncorroborated` and dispatches nothing.
- Negative/regression:
  - if no run is found and channels do not verify, reconcile still returns 3 and dispatches exactly one recovery;
  - recovery-run correlation, mismatched-ref rejection, oversized pagination, schema fail-closed and grace-window tests pass unchanged;
  - `status` mode behaviour is unchanged apart from the new marker.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile-channels.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`

## Related

- GH#33069 (t18554): release shallow-store preflight, which comes from the same v3.37.31 release session.
- `a0130fb9ef` (#32974) added the success grace window that this change complements. That window guards "run found, channels not yet propagated"; this change guards "channels published, run not listed".

title: t18558: fix(prefetch): events tickle 304 must not skip owners whose snapshots are stale (private-org public events feed)
body:
## What

The L1 events tickle in the batch prefetch (`_cmd_refresh`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh:1096-1105`) skips every refresh for an owner whenever `events_tickle` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-events-tickle.sh:218-312`) returns a 304. For organisations it polls `/orgs/{org}/events`, and that endpoint lists **public events only**. On an org whose pulse repos are private, the ETag therefore never changes, the tickle reports "fresh" indefinitely, and that owner's canonical issue/PR snapshots are never refreshed, however old they get.

## Why (evidence)

Measured on 2026-09-29 on a maintainer install with one private-repo organisation (`<private-org>`) among four pulse owners:

- The `<private-org>` ETag file under `~/.aidevops/cache/pulse-events-etag/` last changed on 2026-08-19. `pulse.log` has 48 `fresh for owner=<private-org>` entries and zero `stale` entries. The org's pulse repo is private.
- `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh status` shows that org's issues snapshot STALE since 2026-09-07 and its PR snapshot STALE since 2026-09-11. Every other pulse owner was refreshed at 19:06–19:09Z. Refresh summaries consistently log `tickle_fresh=1 tickle_stale=3`.
- Cost 1 (API volume): each cycle, consumers fall back to a live `_prefetch_single_repo: full sweep` for the private repo, which makes non-conditional list reads, instead of zero-cost conditional 304s.
- Cost 2 (dispatch time, #32638): the cross-cycle worker-draft negative cache from #33044 (`_dispatch_negative_pr_fingerprint`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:118-131`) needs a complete PR snapshot less than 900 s old, so it can never record that repo's draft checkpoints. Over the last 12 h, five issues in the private repo, each blocked by `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT`, were re-rejected 17–19 times each, costing 6.6–10.9 min of dedup ceremony per issue. Candidates rejected at least 5 times without ever launching accounted for 75% of all `dedup_check` time (160.9 min in total). Draft checkpoints on the user-owned repos in the same window *were* cached (`cross-cycle ownership block:worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked`, e.g. for aidevops #33048 and #32446).

## How

1. In `pulse-events-tickle.sh`, record why the tickle returned 0 in a new global, `_PULSE_EVENTS_TICKLE_LAST_REASON`: `etag` (304) or `cooldown` (preflight, rate-limited response, or rate-limited org retry). Reset it at the start of each call.
2. In `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh`, let `_resolve_cache_snapshot` take an optional max-age argument (default unchanged: `PULSE_PREFETCH_FULL_SWEEP_INTERVAL`). Add `_owner_snapshots_recent <slugs>`, which requires every owner slug's issues and PR snapshots to be a hit within `PULSE_EVENTS_TICKLE_MAX_CACHE_AGE` (default 900 s, the same as the dispatch fingerprint bound).
3. In `_cmd_refresh`, honour a tickle skip only for `cooldown`, or when `_owner_snapshots_recent` passes. Otherwise log `events tickle fresh ... but snapshots older than ...s — refreshing`, move that owner from the fresh counter to the stale counter, and run the normal conditional-REST refresh.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-events-tickle.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-batch-prefetch-conditional-rest.sh

## Reference pattern

Stale-snapshot handling in `_resolve_cache_snapshot` (`pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh:1138-1205`). The cooldown-skip semantics in `events_tickle` stay unchanged.

## Acceptance

- If the ETag returns 304 but the owner's snapshots are older than the bound, refresh runs conditional REST for that owner and restamps its snapshots.
- If the ETag returns 304 and all owner snapshots are recent, refresh still skips that owner (no repo calls).
- A cooldown skip still suppresses fanout regardless of snapshot age.
- After deploy, `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh status` shows the private-org snapshots FRESH, and `cross-cycle ownership block:worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` appears for that repo's draft-checkpoint issues.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-batch-prefetch-conditional-rest.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-events-tickle.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-events-tickle.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh`

title: t18559: perf(worktree-cleanup): list open PRs once per local-branch scan and cap per-run GitHub lookups
body:
## What

Make a full-repository `aidevops cleanup local-branches` run cost roughly one open-PR listing per run, not one per branch, and cap its per-branch GitHub lookups so a large backlog is cleared over several bounded runs. Single-branch cleanup after worktree removal keeps its current behaviour and safety.

## Why

- **Observed 2026-09-29 on v3.37.31**, testing the GH#33030 / t18552 helper released in PR #33042:
  - a dry-run on the aidevops repo (3,975 local branches, 12 open PRs) classified branches correctly but scanned only 199 branches in 555s (about 2.8s per branch);
  - a full dry-run would take about 3 hours, with a comparable `--apply`, and issue roughly 2 REST calls per branch, around 8,000 calls, against a 5,000/hour budget shared with pulse and workers.
- **Root cause: `pr_evidence` (`.agents/scripts/local-branch-cleanup-helper.sh:89-124`) re-lists open PRs for every branch.**
  - L97-107 fetch `pulls?state=open&per_page=100&page=N` on every call, and `scan_branch` (L189-218) calls it for every ref from `main` (L231-233). The process list showed the same `pulls?state=open&per_page=100&page=1` request running through `gh-transport-governor.py` for each branch.
  - That listing is loop-invariant within a scan.
  - `active_branch` (L126-131) likewise runs `git worktree list --porcelain` once per branch.
- **The per-branch design is still right for single-branch runs.** `worktree-helper-cmds.sh:342-343` and `worktree-clean-lib.sh:1593-1594` call `--branch <name> --apply` once per removed worktree, so those paths are already bounded.
- **The scoped runs worked.** `--branch 25708 --apply` deleted a squash-merged branch (audit seq 22253), `--branch auto-20260428-030312-gh3305 --apply` deleted an ancestry-merged branch (seq 22254), and `--branch 25710 --apply` preserved an unmerged branch.

## How

1. In `.agents/scripts/local-branch-cleanup-helper.sh`, add a `load_open_pr_refs` function that fetches the open-PR pages once (using the same ≤10-page, fail-closed rules as L97-108) into a global newline-delimited `OPEN_PR_REFS`, with `OPEN_PR_STATUS=ok|unavailable` and an `OPEN_PR_LOADED_AT` epoch.
   - `pr_evidence` reads the cache and reloads only when `OPEN_PR_LOADED_AT` is older than `AIDEVOPS_LOCAL_BRANCH_CLEANUP_OPEN_TTL_S` (default 60, validated `^[1-9][0-9]*$`).
   - `unavailable` still maps to `PR_STATUS=unavailable`, which means keep the branch.
   - The pre-delete recheck in `delete_branch` (L170-175) keeps calling `pr_evidence`, so it is TTL-fresh rather than per-branch.
2. Cache `repo_git worktree list --porcelain` once for the scan in `active_branch`. Keep a fresh, uncached read in `delete_branch` (L166), because it is local and is the mutation-time guard.
3. Add `--max-lookups N` (default 500, validated). This counts only the closed-PR `head=` queries at L112-121. Once the budget is spent, `scan_branch` reports `keep <branch> lookup budget exhausted`, and ancestry-merged branches (L199-201) still proceed because they need no closed-PR lookup. Add a final summary line: `summary scanned=<n> would-delete|deleted=<n> kept=<n> lookups=<n> budget_exhausted=<n>`.
4. Update `usage` (L20-25) and `.agents/workflows/worktree-cleanup.md:148` to describe `--max-lookups`, the TTL variable, and "rerun to continue a large backlog".
5. Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-local-branch-cleanup-helper.sh`:
   - make the `gh` stub (L55-62) append each call to a log file;
   - after the existing dry-run (L67), assert that exactly one `pulls?state=open&` call was made for the whole multi-branch scan;
   - add a `--max-lookups 0` dry-run asserting `would-delete merged` (ancestry, needing no lookup) and `keep squash lookup budget exhausted`;
   - keep every existing assertion (open/fork PR, unavailable evidence, lease race, transport cleanup) unchanged.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/local-branch-cleanup-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-local-branch-cleanup-helper.sh
- .agents/workflows/worktree-cleanup.md
- TODO.md

## Acceptance

- A full dry-run makes one open-PR listing per TTL window, not one per branch. The stub call log shows exactly one `pulls?state=open&` call for the test repository scan.
- `--max-lookups N` bounds closed-PR queries. Branches beyond the budget are kept with `lookup budget exhausted`, and ancestry-merged branches are still reported or deleted.
- Negative/regression:
  - open or fork PR refs are still kept;
  - failed or incomplete GitHub evidence still preserves branches;
  - the moved-ref lease still refuses deletion;
  - no transport worktree is left registered;
  - single-branch `--branch NAME --apply` output is unchanged for the worktree-removal callers.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/local-branch-cleanup-helper.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-local-branch-cleanup-helper.sh`

title: feat(session): numbered y/n and a/b/c asks in What next block
body:
## Problem

title: fix(approval): trusted post-approval comments must not stale locked issue approvals
body:
## Problem

Signed issue approvals go stale whenever **any** new human comment is posted after signing, unless its text exactly matches one of a few hard-coded writer formats in `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh` (`_approval_snapshot_v2_comments_json`). Each new framework or maintainer comment type has needed its own exclusion regex: #28968, #29009, #30127, #30454, #31550, #32455, #32467, and currently #32946 (posting a review after signing stales it).

The longer an approved issue waits for implementation, the more comments pile up, so slow maintainer turnaround makes staleness near-certain. Re-signing needs `sudo` and a human at the terminal.

## Root cause

`_approval_verify_locked_issue_continuity` (`.agents/scripts/approval-helper-continuity.sh`) tolerates drift only in lifecycle metadata (allowlisted labels and assignees changed by write-authorized actors). Every post-approval comment is scope-bearing, whoever wrote it.

## Design: authority equivalence

The approval certifies **untrusted** content for automated work. Approval locks the issue, so after signing only users with write access can comment at all. A comment posted after the approval anchor by a user whose live repository permission is `admin`, `maintain` or `write` confers no authority that user lacks: they could file the same content as a new maintainer-authored issue, which needs no approval.

Under this design, continuity verification should:

- **Exclude** comments created strictly after the approval comment (higher comment ID) whose author is a `User` with live `admin`/`maintain`/`write` permission (`_approval_continuity_actor_authorized`). This is checked through the permission API, never through `author_association`.
- **Keep bound** everything else: title, body, pre-approval comments (including edits to them), comments from read/triage users or unverifiable authors, and linked references.
- **Accept comment-only drift.** When the lifecycle labels and assignees are unchanged, comment-only drift passes, and any lifecycle mutations in the timeline still replay through the existing authorization loop.
- **Fail closed** on permission API errors (`API_ERROR`) and on unlock or relock (the lock-anchor check is unchanged).

PR approvals remain head-SHA and content bound. The existing canonical-writer regexes stay for backward compatibility, but new comment types no longer need them.

Follow-up (not in this change): trusted **body** edits after approval (for example brief enrichment of Files Scope) still stale an approval. Supporting them safely requires per-component digests in the signed payload.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/approval-helper-continuity.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh`
- `.agents/workflows/review-issue-pr.md`

## Verification

`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh`, with new cases:

- Write-authorized maintainer prose after signing → `VERIFIED`.
- Read-permission or external comment after signing → `STALE_APPROVAL`.
- Edited pre-approval comment → `STALE_APPROVAL`.
- Permission API failure → `API_ERROR`.
- Trusted comment combined with a lifecycle transition → `VERIFIED`.

Also run ShellCheck on the touched scripts, plus the other `test-approval-*` suites.

Supersedes #32946 (its observed failure disappears once maintainer review comments no longer stale approvals).

title: feat(approval): keep locked issue approvals valid across write-authorized title/body edits
body:
## Problem

After #33089 (PR #33091), comments that write-authorized users post after the approval no longer stale a locked issue's approval. Edits to the issue **title or body** still do, even when a maintainer makes them. A common example is enriching the brief with `### Files Scope` or a reproducer after approval. That edit forces a `sudo aidevops approve` re-sign, which needs the maintainer at a terminal. A slow reply then blocks dispatch.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** approve an issue from an external author with `sudo aidevops approve issue N owner/repo`. As the maintainer, edit the issue body to add a `### Files Scope` section. Then run `approval-helper.sh verify issue N owner/repo`.

**Actual output:** `STALE_APPROVAL` (exit 4).

**Expected:** `VERIFIED` when every post-approval edit to the title or body was authored by a user with live `admin`/`maintain`/`write` permission.

## Root cause

`_approval_verify_locked_issue_continuity` (`.agents/scripts/approval-helper-continuity.sh`) rebuilds a candidate snapshot and compares its digest against the single signed `snapshot_digest`. The title and body are hashed together with everything else, so any edit changes the digest. The verifier also cannot tell who made the edit: REST exposes no editor identity for issue bodies.

## Proposed design

1. **Editor identity.** Fetch `userContentEdits` for the issue through GraphQL (`issue(number:) { userContentEdits(first:100) { nodes { editor { login } editedAt } } }`). Accept the edit history only if every edit after the approval comment's `created_at` has an editor with live `admin`/`maintain`/`write` permission, checked with `_approval_continuity_actor_authorized`. Fail closed with `API_ERROR` on a missing editor, a deleted-user (`ghost`) editor, pagination beyond one page, or any GraphQL error.
2. **Comparison without re-signing.** Current payloads contain only the whole-snapshot digest, so the verifier has two options for comparing everything except the title and body:
   - Option A: replace `.title` and `.body` in the candidate with the values from the approved snapshot. This requires the signed payload to carry the original title and body, or their hashes, so it only works for future signatures.
   - Option B: add per-component digests to new `aidevops-approval/v2` payloads (for example `issue.content_digests.{title,body,comments,linked_references}`). Keep verifying existing payloads exactly as before.

   Option B is preferred. It is additive, and old signatures keep today's behaviour.
3. **What stays unchanged.** Untrusted edits, edits made before the approval, unlock/relock, and all PR approvals keep their current binding.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/approval-helper-continuity.sh`

## What

`aidevops repos migrate-layout apply` refuses with `OpenCode database verification failed: <isolated opencode.db>` after the repository move and main DB update, leaving a partial receipt.

## Why (root cause, verified)

`plan_consumers` records every isolated `opencode-interactive/*/opencode/opencode.db` as a database consumer, including ones with zero matching rows (drift guard). For those, `changes == []`. - Verify: `python3 tests/test-repo-layout-migrate.py` (existing suite); resume the partial receipt with the same plan/confirm.

## Acceptance

title: t18562: fix(worker): route unverified post-PR handoff with durable PR to checkpoint, ...
body:
## What

A headless worker that exits with a `POST_PR_HANDOFF` signal after opening a ready PR that uses a non-closing reference (`For #N` / `Part of #N`), or a ready PR still missing its `MERGE_SUMMARY`, is routed as a failure today:

- the claim is released with `worker_post_pr_handoff_unverified`;
- fast-fail is reported with crash type `overwhelmed`, which escalates the tier at threshold 1 and posts "could not produce commits" / "failed to produce a PR";
- the issue returns to `status:available` with `auto-dispatch`, so pulse redispatches while the PR is still open.

Route these exact-head durable PR states through the existing checkpoint preservation handlers instead.

## Why

Observed on a managed app repo on 2026-09-28 and 2026-09-29. Two worker runs on one issue both exited 0 with `result=post_pr_handoff` in `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`. Each opened a valid ready PR with a non-closing reference, because part of the scope needed maintainer credentials. Both PRs later merged.

- Each run was released as `worker_post_pr_handoff_unverified`.
- The first run posted a false "Cascade Tier Escalation: tier:standard → tier:thinking" comment.
- The issue stayed `status:available` + `auto-dispatch`, so a third worker was dispatched and self-terminated as a redundant redispatch.

### Root cause

`_hrw_finish_success_run` in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh` has a `post_pr_handoff` gate (about line 2237). The gate calls `_worker_post_pr_handoff_confirmed`, which accepts only state `ready`.

`_pr_handoff_state_for_branch_or_issue` in `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh` never returns `ready` for these PRs:

- `For` / `Ref` PRs get `ready_missing_linkage` (`_pr_handoff_has_linked_issue` accepts only closing keywords).
- PRs without a merge summary get `ready_missing_summary`.

The gate therefore hard-fails and sets `release_needed=0`. The later `_worker_produced_output` switch never runs, although it already preserves `ready_missing_linkage`, `ready_missing_summary` and `draft_checkpoint` as `status:in-review` with `auto-dispatch` removed and the runner assigned. That is the designed exact-head continuation state.

## How

1. In `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`, when `_hrw_finish_success_run` sees an unconfirmed `post_pr_handoff`, classify with `_worker_produced_output` first.
   - For `draft_checkpoint`, `ready_missing_summary` and `ready_missing_linkage`, call the existing `_hrw_preserve_*_handoff` helper and skip fast-fail and tier escalation.
   - Every other class keeps the existing `worker_post_pr_handoff_unverified` failure path, including fail-open `pr_exists`, `noop`, `closed_unmerged`, `unverified_open_pr` and `head_mismatch`.
   - Put this in a small extracted helper so `_hrw_finish_success_run` does not grow.
2. In `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-checkpoint-tests.sh`, add a case for an unverified `post_pr_handoff` with `ready_missing_linkage`. Model it on `test_ready_missing_summary_preserves_in_review_handoff`.
3. In `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-completion-tests.sh`, pin the existing "unverified POST_PR_HANDOFF cannot suppress failure routing" case to a non-durable class (`pr_exists`), so it does not depend on live GitHub classification.

### Reference pattern

Model on `_hrw_preserve_ready_missing_linkage_handoff` and the `ready_missing_linkage)` arm of the `_worker_produced_output` switch in the same function.

## Acceptance

- [ ] An unverified `post_pr_handoff` with `ready_missing_linkage` records `deferred|worker.deferred|checkpointed|worker_ready_missing_linkage`, returns 0 and never calls `_report_failure_to_fast_fail`.
- [ ] The existing "unverified POST_PR_HANDOFF cannot suppress failure routing" test still passes, so non-durable classes still fail.
- [ ] ShellCheck is clean on the changed files.

## Verification

The checkpoint and completion test files are sourced by `test-headless-runtime-helper.sh`.

title: fix(headless): Claude runtime sandbox skips signing/Git-auth env normalization
body:
## What

The Claude headless runtime path builds the sandbox passthrough without first normalizing the worker's process-scoped signing and Git-auth environment. The OpenCode path does this; the Claude path does not.

Found while implementing #33064 (PR #33116).

## Evidence

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-invoke.sh:239-249` (`_invoke_opencode_run_sandboxed`) calls `prepare_headless_signing_sandbox_env "$runtime_role"` and `prepare_headless_git_auth_sandbox_env "$runtime_role"`, failing with exit 87/88 if either cannot be isolated.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh:357-359` (`_invoke_claude`) calls `build_sandbox_passthrough_csv` directly, with no provider or role arguments and neither prepare function.
- `build_sandbox_passthrough_csv` (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh:904-908`) forwards `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0..2`/`GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0..2` only when `_headless_signing_sandbox_env_is_normalized` holds (`_AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_SIGNING_GIT_CONFIG_START == 0`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT == 3`), and the Git-auth variables only when `_headless_git_auth_sandbox_env_is_normalized` holds.

Effect: when the launcher has any ambient `GIT_CONFIG_*` entry before the signing entries (start > 0), a Claude worker gets no dedicated signing config inside the sandbox. It then falls back to the global signing key and can fail at commit, which is the #33064 failure mode through a different route. Git-auth isolation is likely affected in the same way. This is a static trace; it has not been reproduced on a live Claude worker.

## Reproducer

Unconfirmed investigation from a static trace. To reproduce: with `commit.gpgsign=true`, a dedicated key from `aidevops signing headless-setup`, and one ambient `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1`/`GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0` exported in the launcher, dispatch a worker on the Claude runtime. Expected on current `main`: the sandbox receives no `GIT_CONFIG_*`, so the worker signs with the global (interactive) key and fails at commit. The OpenCode runtime under the same setup signs correctly.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-contract-tests.sh`

## Fix

In `_invoke_claude` (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`), before `build_sandbox_passthrough_csv`, call `prepare_headless_signing_sandbox_env worker` and `prepare_headless_git_auth_sandbox_env worker` with the same fail-closed exit codes (87/88) and messages as `_invoke_opencode_run_sandboxed`. Check whether `build_sandbox_passthrough_csv` should receive the provider/role arguments the OpenCode path passes. The comment at `headless-runtime-worker.sh:333-335` says a second `_invoke_claude` copy may exist in `headless-runtime-helper.sh`; apply the fix to every live copy.

## Verification

body:
## Description

The interactive `What next` block can report both `Needed from you: None` and
`Left to capture: None` while session-owned changes remain uncommitted in a
linked worktree and the runtime requires explicit commit approval.

This creates a false ready-to-close signal. A user following it can close the

work easy to overlook or lose.

## Root cause

The session policy requires a general capture check but does not explicitly

- `.agents/reference/session.md`
- focused regression coverage under `tests/`

- Before returning control, interactive sessions inspect live Git status in

- Session-owned modified, staged, or untracked files are reported under

- If commit approval is required and absent, the approval appears under
  `Needed from you` and `Close` remains `Not yet`.
- Earlier status snapshots cannot satisfy the final capture check.

title: Pulse: per-class dispatch cap (max share of worker slots for a labelled issue class)
body:
## What

Let a project cap how much of a machine's worker capacity one class of issues may use, for example "award-enrichment issues may use at most 50% of this machine's simultaneous worker slots".

Proposed shape (implementer may refine):

- A label such as `dispatch-class:<name>` on issues.
- Per-repo config in `repos.json` (or `.aidevops.json`): `"dispatch_classes": { "award-enrichment": { "max_share_pct": 50 } }`, with an optional absolute `max_workers`.
- In the Pulse dispatch loop, before launching a worker for an issue with a class label, count active workers for issues of the same class (from the shared worker discovery path) and skip the issue when `active >= floor(simultaneous_target_final * max_share_pct / 100)` (minimum 1). Log the skip reason in `pulse.log` and the dashboard.

## Why

Observed on 2026-09-30 while preparing a batch of about 50 data-only award-enrichment issues (project repo, product class):

- `pulse.log` `Dispatch_capacity` reports `simultaneous_target_final=8` on this machine.
- `pulse-capacity-alloc.sh` provides product/tooling class reservations (`PRODUCT_MIN=5`, `TOOLING_MAX=3`) and a `check_repo_worker_cap` function (default `MAX_WORKERS_PER_REPO=5`), but the only caller of `check_repo_worker_cap` is the `repo-cap` CLI command in `pulse-wrapper-commands.sh:87`; the dispatch loop does not use it. There is no per-label or per-class cap.
- Result: a large batch of `auto-dispatch` issues of one kind can occupy every product slot on every maintainer machine, starving feature and bug work in the same repo. The only current workaround is manual drip-feeding of `auto-dispatch` labels.

The maintainer asked for enrichment to use "up to 50% of available concurrency".

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity-alloc.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md`

(Exact dispatch-loop file may differ; locate the loop that launches workers after `Dispatch_capacity` is computed.)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With `max_share_pct: 50` and `simultaneous_target_final=8`, at most 4 workers run for issues labelled with that class; other issues in the same repo still dispatch into the remaining slots.
- [ ] Issues without a class label behave exactly as today.
- [ ] Skips are logged with class, active count and cap.
- [ ] Documented in `reference/worker-diagnostics.md` next to the minimum concurrency floor.

## Verification

- Existing pulse dispatch test harness (for example `tests/test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh`) extended with a class-cap case.
- `shellcheck` on changed scripts.

title: Project single status:blocked for open terminal-blocker circuits and release it on trusted retry
body:
## What

When a terminal-blocker circuit opens or is already open, the release path still projects `status:available`, contradicting the circuit's "Projected state: status:blocked" text and leaving dual-status issues (reported in #33025 follow-up comments: an issue temporarily carried both `status:available` and `status:blocked`). Project exactly one `status:blocked` while a known-class circuit is open, and return the issue to `status:available` when a trusted OWNER/MEMBER `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` directive (or a relevant revision) re-arms dispatch.

## Why

Found during #33025 and blocked by #33025: start after its PR merges, because this builds on its collaborator-runner hold evidence in `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`. The circuit now engages for collaborator runners (#33025), but label state still says the issue is available while dispatch is held, which misleads operators and other tooling. `status:blocked` is also a hard pre-claim gate (`_dispatch_preclaim_brief_scope_verdict` in `pulse-dispatch-core.sh`), so projecting it without an automatic release on retry would break the documented retry-only recovery — both halves must ship together.

## Reproducer

Static code-path evidence on `main` at `cdcfe21` (confirmed by reading source, not yet reproduced on a live issue):

1. `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh:375` writes the circuit comment with `Projected state: status:blocked.`
2. `headless-runtime-failure.sh` `_hrff_handle_terminal_blocker_release` (`circuit` and `open` branches, ~L606-620) then calls `_hrff_release_rate_limit_circuit_cleanup` -> `clear_active_status_on_release`.
3. `shared-constants.sh` `clear_active_status_on_release` (~L1436-1455) projects `available` when no linked PR exists, so a circuit-held issue with no PR ends up labelled `status:available` while dispatch is suppressed.

## How

- `headless-runtime-failure.sh` `_hrff_handle_terminal_blocker_release`: in `circuit`/`open` modes, replace the `_hrff_release_rate_limit_circuit_cleanup` → `clear_active_status_on_release` (projects `available`) call with a single-status `set_issue_status ... blocked` projection plus assignee removal and unlock.
- Add a release path: when `terminal_blocker_circuit_active` stops being active for an issue labelled `status:blocked` whose newest blocked reason is a terminal-blocker circuit (not a brief hold, dependency, permission-helper or other hold), project `status:available` once. Candidate owner: `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` `_tbr_check_entry` (already detects re-arm and retires the queue entry) — verify it runs on every runner that opened a circuit.
- Keep `needs-maintainer-permissions` reserved for `worker-permission-helper.sh` requests (see `_hrff_apply_terminal_permission_hold`).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`

## Acceptance

- Opening or hitting an open circuit leaves exactly one status label: `status:blocked`.
- A trusted OWNER/MEMBER retry directive (or relevant code/brief revision for non-permission classes) returns the issue to `status:available` without manual label edits; collaborator retries do not.
- Unknown-class blockers keep today's retryable behaviour (no durable hold).
- Brief holds, dependency blocks and permission-helper holds are never released by this path.

## Verification

`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-release-unlock.sh` (note: its draft-checkpoint case fails identically on main as of cdcfe21), and `shellcheck -x` on modified files.

title: claim-task-id: reconcile fetch omits --depth=1 in isolated counter context and times out on large repos
body:
## What

`claim-task-id.sh` fails with `UNRECOVERABLE_COUNTER_DESYNC: cannot fetch origin/<branch> for reconciliation` on large repositories. The reconcile fetch skips the `--depth=1` that every other fetch in the isolated counter context uses, so it transfers full branch history and exceeds `CAS_HTTPS_TIMEOUT_S` (default 30s) on both HTTPS and the SSH fallback.

## Evidence

On a large private project repo (counter branch = default branch `develop`), run twice with defaults:

```text
[INFO] Using isolated Git context for canonical counter discovery and CAS
[INFO] AIDEVOPS_TASK_COUNTER_STATUS=reconciling detail=branch=origin/develop
[WARN] git timed out after 30s on HTTPS — retrying via SSH (...)
[WARN] SSH fallback also timed out after 30s — both transports unavailable
[ERROR] UNRECOVERABLE_COUNTER_DESYNC: cannot fetch origin/develop for reconciliation
```

With `CAS_HTTPS_TIMEOUT_S=180`, the same command succeeded (`recovered_contention detail=refetched`, claim in 0s). A normal `git fetch origin develop` from a linked worktree of the same repo finishes quickly, because that object store already holds the history.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh`:

- `_cas_fetch_counter_branch_for_reconcile()` (around line 701) runs `fetch -q "$REMOTE_NAME" "$COUNTER_BRANCH"` with no depth limit and no `--no-tags`.
- The other isolated-context fetches already use `_counter_context_is_isolated && depth_args=(--depth=1)` (around lines 506, 747 and 1139). The comment at line 503 explains why: depth is limited to the isolated bare context, so the shared object store is never made shallow.
- Also audit the other fetches without a depth limit, around lines 851 and 906 (`fetch -q "$REMOTE_NAME" "$COUNTER_BRANCH"`), for the same gap.

## How

- Apply the same `depth_args` pattern and `--no-tags` in `_cas_fetch_counter_branch_for_reconcile()`. Keep the explicit remote-tracking refspec form used at line 508 if the later reconcile code reads `refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>`.
- Apply the same fix to the other isolated-context fetches found in the audit. Never add depth when the context is not isolated.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Every fetch in the isolated counter context uses `--depth=1 --no-tags`. Non-isolated fetches are unchanged.
- [ ] The reconcile path completes within the default 30s on a repo with deep history.
- [ ] The shared object store never gains a `shallow` file (existing invariant, line 503).

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-https-ssh-fallback.sh
```

title: planning-publisher: pre-commit validation diffs temp index against stale worktree HEAD, so upstream files block planning commits
body:
## What

`planning-commit-helper.sh` can refuse a TODO.md-only change because of files it never touched. The planning publisher builds a temporary index from the fresh remote tip (`parent_sha`), then runs `pre-commit-hook.sh` against that index. The hook's staged-file detection (`git diff --cached`) compares the index with the worktree's `HEAD`, not with `parent_sha`. When `HEAD` lags the remote, every upstream change since `HEAD` looks staged, and the hook validates or blocks those files.

## Evidence

In a linked worktree of a private project repo, the worktree was created from `origin/develop`. Then `develop` gained a commit that changed `.github/workflows/security.yml` (adding a self-hosted runner label unknown to actionlint). The only local change was one added TODO.md line (`git status --short` → ` M TODO.md`).

```text
[plan] Planning files to commit:
  - TODO.md
[INFO] Checking staged GitHub Actions workflow files...
[INFO] Linting 1 workflow file(s) with actionlint...
[ERROR] Workflow lint FAILED: .github/workflows/security.yml
...
[plan] Planning publication validation failed; nothing pushed
```

After `git merge --ff-only origin/develop` in the worktree, so that `HEAD` equals the remote tip, the same command passed and published directly.

## Root cause

- `.agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh`: `_planning_publish_build_index` (around line 516) runs `read-tree "$parent_sha"`. `_planning_publish_validate` (around line 596) then runs `GIT_INDEX_FILE="$index_file" HOOK_MODE=pre-commit "$hook"` without telling the hook what the base is.
- `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh` derives staged files from plain `git diff --cached`, which diffs against `HEAD`. Examples: `check_workflow_files` (around line 1082), the shell-file list (around line 58), TODO checks (around lines 86, 541, 550, 558, 704, 719, 727), counter (136), the general list (475) and new root files (1037).

Any failing check can be triggered this way, not only actionlint. Upstream ShellCheck or root-file findings would block planning publication in the same way, whenever the worktree is behind.

## How

- Add an optional base override to the hook. For example, when `AIDEVOPS_PRE_COMMIT_BASE` is set, staged-file helpers use `git diff --cached <base>`. Route all `git diff --cached` call sites through one helper so none are missed.
- In `_planning_publish_validate`, pass `AIDEVOPS_PRE_COMMIT_BASE="$parent_sha"` alongside `GIT_INDEX_FILE`.
- Ordinary `git commit` behaviour, with no override, is unchanged.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A planning publication from a worktree whose `HEAD` lags the remote validates only the planning paths it changes.
- [ ] A planning change that itself breaks a check still fails validation.
- [ ] Normal pre-commit runs are unaffected.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh .agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-publisher.sh
```

Add a regression to `test-planning-publisher.sh` in which the remote tip changes a non-planning file that fails a hook check, while the worktree `HEAD` lags.

title: claim-task-id: reconcile seeds from stale local TODO.md, and a foreign-title tNNN prefix match is reported as recovery (ID collision)
body:
## What

`claim-task-id.sh` allocated two task IDs that were already in use, one after the other. Each time it found the other session's issue by `tNNN:` prefix, reported it as "recovered", created nothing, and burned the ID. A third run was needed to get a free ID.

## Evidence

The project repo uses the counter on its default branch `develop`, with an isolated counter context. Counter history on the remote:

```text
02:16:49 chore: claim t18413
02:40:04 chore: reconcile task counter (18414->18419)
02:40:09 chore: claim t18419
```

Between 02:16 and 02:40, another session created t18414–t18420 (issues and TODO rows) without advancing `.task-counter`. The next claims then did this:

```text
Counter at 18419, claiming t18419..t18419, new counter: 18420
Found existing OPEN issue #<A> with exact t18419 prefix, skipping duplicate creation
Recovered issue #<A>, but publication:pending could not be verified
Issue creation failed for t18419 (non-fatal — ID is secured)
--- rerun ---
Counter at 18420, claiming t18420..t18420, new counter: 18421
Found existing OPEN issue #<B> with exact t18420 prefix, skipping duplicate creation
```

Issue #<A> is titled "t18419: <another session's feature>" and my requested title was "ci: declare …". The titles are unrelated, yet the collision was treated as a recovery. The remote `develop:TODO.md` already contained t18419 and t18420 at that time.

## Root causes

1. **The reconcile floor reads a stale local file.** `_compute_counter_seed()` in `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh` (around line 1028) reads `${repo_path}/TODO.md` from the working tree. When `repo_path` is the canonical checkout, which is a read-only mirror that lags the remote, the seed misses recently published IDs. Reconcile around line 767 then sets the counter below IDs that are already taken. It should read `TODO.md` from the fetched remote counter branch ref (`git show <remote>/<branch>:TODO.md`) that reconcile already has.
2. **Foreign-title prefix matches count as success.** `_check_duplicate_issue()` in `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-issue.sh` (around lines 416–431) returns any open issue whose title starts with `tNNN: `. On a new allocation, a match whose title differs from the requested title is an ID collision, not an idempotent retry. It should fail loudly, for example with `TASK_ID_COLLISION`, and ideally bump the counter past the colliding ID and retry, instead of reporting `Recovered issue`.
3. **Undetected: the allocator that skipped the counter.** Some path created t18414–t18420 without CAS-advancing `.task-counter`. The creating path is unknown from this session. Check `issue-sync-helper.sh` push/allocation and `planning-commit-helper.sh next_task_id --offline` for writes of a `tNNN` that bypass the counter.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The reconcile seed uses the remote branch's `TODO.md` and ignores the local working tree.
- [ ] A new allocation whose `tNNN:` issue already exists with a different title does not report recovery. It either retries with the next free ID or fails with an explicit collision status.
- [ ] Idempotent retries (same title) still recover the existing issue.
- [ ] Finding 3 is investigated. Either fix the bypassing path or record which path it was.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh .agents/scripts/claim-task-id-issue.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-no-orphan.sh
```

title: scope-guard-pre-push compares against stale local main instead of origin/main
body:
## Observed

`scope-guard-pre-push.sh` blocked a new-branch push in a linked worktree and listed
files that were already merged to `origin/main` by an earlier PR. The branch
itself changed only two in-scope files (`git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD`).

## Cause

`_compute_baseline()` (`.agents/hooks/scope-guard-pre-push.sh`, around lines
231-257) reads `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, then strips the `refs/remotes/origin/`
prefix with `sed`, leaving the bare name `main`. `git merge-base HEAD main` then
uses the local `main` branch, which is often stale in a canonical checkout that
sessions must not update. Every file merged upstream since that stale local
`main` is counted as out of scope.

## Fix

Keep the remote-qualified ref (for example `origin/main`) for `merge-base`: strip
only `refs/remotes/`, or resolve `refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD` directly. Check
whether `complexity-regression-pre-push.sh`, which the comment says this mirrors
(GH#20045), has the same pattern.

## Verification

Reproduce: a linked worktree whose canonical local `main` is behind
`origin/main`; branch from `origin/main`; commit one in-scope file; push a new
branch. Expected: no out-of-scope files reported.

title: task-id guard flags a valid task ID followed by a sentence period as malformed
body:
## What

`task_identity_has_malformed_candidate` in `.agents/scripts/task-identity-lib.sh` (around line 190) flags a valid task ID followed by a sentence-ending period as malformed. The task-ID collision guard then blocks the commit with `__malformed__ — malformed task identity`.

## Reproduction (observed 2026-09-30, v3.37.34)

Commit body: `... to the PFT overlay, and splits point 5 into t112.` (t112 is a validly claimed ID.)

Result: `[task-id-guard][BLOCK] ... __malformed__ — malformed task identity`. Rewording to `into t112 (brief added)` passes.

## Cause

`candidate_ere` is `[tT][0123456789][[:alnum:].-]*`. It includes `.` in the continuation class, so the trailing sentence period becomes part of the candidate (`t112.`), which fails `task_identity_validate`. The design comment at line ~133 intentionally treats dots as non-boundaries to catch truncated IDs such as `t7.0`, but a dot followed by whitespace or end of text is ordinary punctuation.

## Suggested fix

Before validating, strip one trailing `.` from the candidate when it is followed by whitespace or end of text. Keep rejecting inner dots (`t7.0`, `t7.x`).

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/task-identity-lib.sh` (`task_identity_has_malformed_candidate`, and `task_identity_extract_first`/`extract_all` if they share the boundary)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-task-identity-lib.sh` (add: `"split into t112."` is not malformed; `"t7.0 marker"` stays rejected)

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-task-identity-lib.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-task-id-collision-guard.sh
```
